{{Short description|Mathematical theorem}}
In [[algebraic geometry]], '''Lange's conjecture''' is a theorem about stability of [[vector bundle]]s over curves, introduced by {{ill|Herbert_Lange_(mathematician)|lt=Herbet Lange|de|Herbert_Lange_(Mathematiker)|vertical-align=sup}}<ref>{{harvs|txt|last=Lange|first=Herbert|year=1983}}</ref> and proved by [[Montserrat Teixidor i Bigas]] and [[Barbara Russo]] in 1999.

==Statement==
Let ''C'' be a smooth projective [[algebraic curve|curve]] of [[Genus (mathematics)#Algebraic geometry|genus]] greater or equal to 2. For [[generic property|generic]] vector bundles <math>E_1</math> and <math>E_2</math> on ''C'' of ranks and degrees <math>(r_1, d_1)</math> and <math>(r_2, d_2)</math>, respectively, a generic extension
:<math>0 \to E_1 \to E \to E_2 \to 0</math>
has ''E'' [[stable vector bundle|stable]] provided that <math>\mu(E_1) < \mu(E_2)</math>, where <math>\mu(E_i) = d_i/r_i</math> is the [[stable vector bundle#Stable vector bundles over curves|slope]] of the respective bundle. The notion of a generic vector bundle here is a generic point in the [[Moduli space#Moduli of vector bundles|moduli space of semistable vector bundles]] on ''C'', and a generic extension is one that corresponds to a generic point in the vector space [[Ext functor|<math>\operatorname{Ext}^1</math>]]<math>(E_2,E_1)</math>.

An original formulation by Lange is that for a pair of integers <math>(r_1, d_1)</math> and <math>(r_2, d_2)</math> such that <math>d_1/ r_1 < d_2/r_2</math>, there exists a [[short exact sequence]] as above with ''E'' stable. This formulation is equivalent because the existence of a short exact sequence like that is an open condition on ''E'' in the moduli space of semistable vector bundles on ''C''.
